doc.title: Dan Wall and Adam Nussbaum interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 19, 2001

title: Dan Wall's early influences: Motown, guitarists, Wes, organ players
summary: Wall describes turning from piano lessons to rock and guitar, then to Wes Montgomery, Tatum, Jimmy Smith and organ trios.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Who are some of the musicians you might have stolen from early on?
Everybody. Only the best. Well I probably stole from some of the worst too.
Or you figure out who you don’t want to steal from along the way too.

That’s basically I think probably what happens really. That doesn’t interest me, I won’t steal from him. Now this over here, yes, let me grab some of that. Well you know I grew up listening to, when I really became interested in music, you know I was telling you about being from the family of pianists, I think that really actually turned me off in the beginning because I hated piano lessons. You know because everybody did that. But they were smart, after about a year they said listen, if you don’t like that you don’t have to do that. That’s the end of that. So then when I went back to it, it was because I got interested in rock & roll. I heard Motown music, I heard the Stones, all these people, and I was dabbling with the piano because my uncle, hearing this great sound, but what I was really interested in was the guitar. Because of that music. So I started listening to guitar players,

of course all of the bands of that time, and the guitar player with James Brown and the whole smear of kind of those two kinds of music, I even had a little period of time where I listened to a lot of country music. And basically because I loved the guitar playing, I loved their sound, I loved their percussive attack and the edge they played with, and I got into a little country thing for a while. But then I kind of gravitated back to the jazz world and I was hearing Wes Montgomery. That’s one of the first, I think Wes Montgomery, Kenny Burrell were two of the first people who really hit me. And around the same time I was paying attention to some piano players because of a record that was in the house and it was a record that was kind of like a variety disk with Tatum, a couple tracks by Tatum, a couple of tracks by Lenny Tristano, a couple tracks Mary Lou Williams. That was pretty amazing to hear all this. And that really kind of grabbed my ear. So it was equally split between guitar players and starting to find out about some of the piano players from that period, Errol Garner was another one. But when I heard the guitar players, especially Wes, then I started hearing Jimmy Smith, and then the organ kind of grabbed my attention. And through him I heard Larry Young and then that led to a whole path of organ players and organ trios with all those great guitar players. But at the same time I kind of kept my interest in rock & roll and Motown. I kept it all going for a while until it became really like yeah I want to play jazz. I said this is really what I feel like, this is the serious thing for me.
